target_customer: Teams and AI-heavy knowledge workers, including on-prem enterprises
problem: Conversations and agent traces across AI tools are siloed and every session starts without prior context.
product_category: AI memory and shared context layer

founders.name: Tiger Wang
founders.background_notes: Linux kernel security research at Yale

technical_complexity.rationale: Syncing many providers and building a live ontology is standard engineering with hard data integration parts.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated team context could lock in users, but model vendors can add memory natively.

market_need_then: Heavy daily AI use by knowledge workers made context loss across tools common; no quantified demand found.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand material found; the name is memorable but shared with other companies in search results.

outcome_analysis: Nessie is a Fall 2025 company run by two Yale graduates and former Amazon engineers, backed by Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund. It is too early for an outcome; the main risk is that model providers ship native cross-tool memory.
notes: UNVERIFIED: CB Insights shows about $500K total raised; round label varies between pre-seed (VCBacked) and seed. BoxGroup and Precursor appear only in the company's own YC description. Competitor sources found (Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, MemoryPlugin) are 2026 articles without dates near 2025 batch, so the list is empty. Name origin not found.
